# Autominer

> Web app that turns a Minecraft screenshot of an amethyst geode into the layout of an automatic amethyst farm: it finds the budding amethyst blocks in the image (camera + block lattice solved from the block edges), then computes, for each axis X/Y/Z, the groups of at most 12 blocks a piston can push, slime or honey for each group, and one flying machine per group. App: https://codeof-diego.github.io/autominer/

Everything runs client-side in JavaScript (WebGL for the 3D view, OpenCV.js from a CDN for the scan). Fetching the HTML alone computes nothing: to use the app you need a real browser (e.g. a headless browser driven by Playwright or Puppeteer, or a browser-use tool). No data is sent to any server; saved geodes stay in the browser's IndexedDB.

## How an agent can use it

1. Open the app URL and wait until the landing page is shown (`document.body.dataset.screen === 'landing'`).
2. Input, one of:
   - a screenshot: set the file input `#photo_input` to a PNG/JPG (e.g. Playwright `page.setInputFiles('#photo_input', path)`). The scan takes a few seconds (longer the first time, while OpenCV.js downloads). It is done when `App.entry.vein` is set; `App.entry.blocks` is the number of budding amethyst blocks found (0 or no vein after ~60 s: the scan failed, usually because the geode is not cleared or is covered by grown buds);
   - a random demo geode: click `[data-action="random"]`;
   - a known geode: open the debug tools (Settings, Debug tools) and paste `{seed, size, ores}` into Import JSON.
3. Steps 1-7 (scan, geode, borders, reachable, groups, materials, machines): call `App.goStep(n)` or press the keys `1`-`7`. The current step's explanation is in `#step_short` and `#step_desc`.
4. Output available today:
   - `App.entry.vein`: the geode as JSON `{seed, size: [x, y, z], ores: [[x, y, z], ...]}`, the budding amethyst cells, 0-based;
   - the farm (steps 3-7) is shown in 3D only. A machine-readable result (every block with position, type and facing, per axis and group, plus a materials list) is planned but not available yet: do not scrape internal variables, they are not a stable interface.

## Limits to report to the user

- Step 7 (flying machines) is a first version and NOT buildable yet: the obsidian anchors are misplaced and machines of different groups may touch.
- Some geodes cannot be split using only slime and honey; far or bud-covered blocks may be missed by the scan (the user can fix them by hand in step 1).
- Vanilla textures only.
